_what_this_is: Recorded answers that the SME seat has individually examined and ruled
FALSE FAILS. `replay_history.py` re-scores every recorded answer with
today's check() and gates on FRAGILE; an entry here tells it that one
named observation's failure is not evidence of non-determinism.
THIS IS AN OVERRIDE LIST, AND OVERRIDE LISTS GET USED. It is a real
reduction in assurance and ADR-0015 records it as one. What keeps it
narrow is that an entry names an ARTIFACT, not a rule:
- `scored_sha256` is the digest of run_evals.flatten_answer(resp) --
the exact text check() scores. A different answer has a different
digest and is NOT admitted, so FRAGILE stays live on precisely the
thing it exists to catch: a NEW disagreement.
- `admits_fails` must match check()'s output EXACTLY. If the same
recorded answer starts failing for a different or additional reason
-- because a token was added, or a check kind changed -- the
admission does not apply and the gate fires. An entry cannot
silence a defect it was not written for.
- It can only ever suppress a verdict that is already FAIL. It cannot
turn a PASS into anything.
- An entry that matches nothing is STALE and FAILS the run, so the
register cannot quietly accumulate dead overrides.
It does NOT change run_evals.py. `make evals` still scores q03 as
failing and the live scorecard still says so; only the merge gate
admits it. The register is about what blocks a merge, not about what
the scorer believes.
Adding an entry requires an SME-seat ruling citing primary evidence a
reader can falsify (ADR-0005). `ruling` must point at that document.
There is one human here, so nothing mechanically enforces that -- which
is exactly the weakness to state rather than paper over.
Audit the true state at any time: replay_history.py --no-admissions

admissions.question: q03
why: The banned literal occurs once, inside the scope of 'I cannot confirm
from these sources whether ...'. The answer attaches ZERO citations to
the other-agency row and explicitly declines, so it does not commit the
error the ban exists to catch -- a TTB proposition carrying a Red No. 3
citation (SME ruling 2026-08-12).
The passing answer at the SAME sha differs only in how the object of
the hedge is phrased: 'whether you must separately update that formula
approval' instead of 'whether TTB requires a formula amendment'. Same
paragraph, same hedge, same empty agency row, same pending_review.
See milestones/M07/q03-prose-diff.txt.
Three candidate instruments were measured before this entry was
written and all three failed (milestones/M07/q03-instrument-probe.txt):
keying on the failure reason collides with three WRONG specimens that
produce byte-identical reason sets; dropping the ban leaks six
defective answers including B1; and the structural row check M05 open
thread 7 proposed cannot discriminate -- the agency row carries zero
citations in the PASSING answers too -- and is inert on 10 of the 22
recorded answers, which carry no answer_rows at all.
So this is not a fix. It is an admission that q03's ban cannot separate
the correct hedge from a flat assertion by any means available here.
check_discrimination.py's LIMIT_FALSE_FAIL specimen stays, so
`make discrimination` keeps reporting the underlying defect.
